summary: Qwen lane, checked live on 2026-11-15. The Hugging Face listing for the Qwen org, sorted by createdAt, shows these open-weight LLM generations in the window: Qwen3.5 (Feb 2026: 0.8B/2B/4B/9B dense, 27B dense, 35B-A3B, 122B-A10B, 397B-A17B, plus official FP8 and GPTQ-Int4 builds), Qwen3-Coder-Next (80B-A3B, Feb 2026), Qwen3.6 (Apr 2026: 27B and 35B-A3B), and Qwen3.8 (Aug 2026: 27B dense, Flash-Next 176B-total/6B-active, 2.4T-A95B) (https://huggingface.co/api/models?author=Qwen&sort=createdAt&direction=-1&limit=200). No Qwen3.7 open weights exist; Qwen3.7-Plus appears only as an API comparison column. Every Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 model is natively vision-language (Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration), thinks by default and can switch thinking off per request with chat_template_kwargs enable_thinking=false. vLLM's `--language-model-only` flag skips the vision encoder. The vLLM recipes for all of them use `--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder --reasoning-parser qwen3` (https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/tree/main/models/Qwen). On this 16 GB RTX 5080 Laptop, the strongest Qwen models do NOT fit in vLLM. Qwen3.8-27B needs 19.5-26.4 GB even at INT4/NVFP4, and its recipe needed `--enforce-eager` and a 32K context to fit on a 32 GB RTX 5090 (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vllm-project/recipes/main/models/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B.yaml). Qwen3.6-35B-A3B NVFP4 is 23.4 GB. So in vLLM the practical Qwen choices are Qwen3.5-4B in BF16 (9.3 GB), a community 4-bit Qwen3.5-9B (about 9.1-9.4 GB), Qwen3-VL-8B-FP8 and the older Qwen3-8B/14B-AWQ. Larger models need llama.cpp or Ollama. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (Q4_K_M 20.5 GB GGUF from ggml-org, 3B active) is the best MoE fit, with some experts kept in RAM through `--n-cpu-moe`. Qwen3.8-27B fits on the GPU only at about 3-bit to IQ4_XS (13.1-14.4 GB, unsloth), or at Q4 with partial offload, which will be slow because the model is dense. Qwen3-Coder-Next (official Q4_K_M GGUF 48.4 GB) is possible only with most experts in system RAM, and that is tight given about 41 GiB of free RAM. Because the 3.5/3.6/3.8 models use hybrid attention (Gated DeltaNet), only 1 in 4 layers keeps a KV cache: 32 KiB/token for 9B, 20 KiB/token for 35B-A3B and 64 KiB/token for 27B at BF16. That makes long contexts cheap compared with Qwen3/Qwen3-Coder-30B. Vendor-reported agentic numbers: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B SWE-bench Verified 73.4 and Terminal-Bench 2.0 51.5; Qwen3.6-27B 77.2 / 59.3; Qwen3.8-27B Terminal-Bench 2.1 73.0 and SWE-bench Pro 61.7; Qwen3-Coder-Next SWE-bench Verified 70.6-71.3 depending on scaffold; Qwen3.5-9B BFCL-V4 66.1 and TAU2 79.1. All are self-reported by Qwen. Non-thinking-only (instruct) Qwen options are Qwen3-Coder-Next, Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct and Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507. Every 3.5+ model is a hybrid that thinks by default.

facts.claim: The Qwen org has no Qwen3.7 repository. The Qwen3.8 open releases are Qwen3.8-27B (2026-08-05), -FP8 (2026-08-13), Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B (+FP8, 2026-08-08) and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (+FP8, 2026-08-24). Qwen3.7-Plus appears only as a benchmark column.

Qwen3.6 has only two open models: 35B-A3B (2026-04-15) and 27B (2026-04-21), each with an official FP8 build. Qwen3.5 (Feb 2026) has 0.8B/2B/4B/9B/27B/35B-A3B/122B-A10B/397B-A17B, with official FP8 and GPTQ-Int4 builds only for 27B and larger.

Qwen3.8-27B is described as 'Causal Language Model with Vision Encoder'. The 3.5/3.6/3.8 configs use Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration with a vision_config, and Qwen publishes no text-only variants. vLLM's --language-model-only flag skips loading the vision encoder to free VRAM for KV cache.

Qwen3.8 thinks by default. Thinking is disabled per request with extra_body chat_template_kwargs {"enable_thinking": false}. reasoning_effort accepts xhigh (default), medium or low, and preserve_thinking is on by default.

The vLLM recipe says --reasoning-parser qwen3 is needed in practice: the template opens every assistant turn with <think>, so without the parser the reasoning lands in message.content. It also says thinking defaults can be set server-wide with --default-chat-template-kwargs.

The vLLM recipe for Qwen3.8-27B uses --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder. A recipe commit on 2026-10-08 switched to qwen3_coder because qwen3_xml broke tool calls on the Rust frontend.
In vLLM main, qwen3_coder and qwen3_xml both map to Qwen3EngineToolParser, and qwen3_json is an alias of hermes for the Qwen2.5/QwQ/Qwen3 JSON tool format.
The Qwen3, Qwen3-30B-A3B and Qwen3-Next vLLM recipes and the Qwen docs use --tool-call-parser hermes for the older Qwen3/Qwen3-Next models, while Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 and Qwen3-Coder use qwen3_coder.

The Qwen3.8-27B recipe gives min_vllm_version 0.17.0 and docker image vllm/vllm-openai:qwen38, which Docker Hub shows last updated 2026-08-12. The latest stable vLLM is v0.32.0 (2026-10-18), and vllm/vllm-openai:latest was updated 2026-11-02.
The Qwen3.6-35B-A3B card recommends vllm>=0.19.0. The Qwen3-Coder-Next card requires vllm>=0.15.0. The nvidia NVFP4 Qwen3.6 builds need vLLM >=0.28.0 per the recipe.

The recipe marks consumer Blackwell (sm120) as verified on 2026-08-15. On sm120 vLLM selects the FlashInferCutlassNvFp4LinearKernel for NVFP4, which is a real kernel and not an emulation. Block-FP8 Qwen3.5-family checkpoints load without disabling DeepGemm.
Even a 32 GB RTX 5090 (31.4 GiB usable) could run Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 only with --enforce-eager and a 32K context; CUDA graph capture hit OOM otherwise. So no 27B Qwen fits a 16 GB GPU under vLLM.
Qwen3.8-27B checkpoint sizes: BF16 55.6 GB, official FP8 30.9 GB, nvidia NVFP4 21.9 GB, Inferact NVFP4 26.4 GB, RedHatAI INT4 19.5 GB, RedHatAI MXFP4 19.8 GB.

Measured from HF blobs: Qwen3.5-4B BF16 9.3 GB; Qwen3.5-9B BF16 19.3 GB; RedHatAI/Qwen3.5-9B-FP8-dynamic 14.0 GB; Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 24.4 GB; nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 23.4 GB; Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 37.5 GB.

Per config.json, only 1 in 4 layers is full attention. BF16 KV per token is 32 KiB for Qwen3.5-4B/9B (8 layers x 4 KV heads x 256 dim), 20 KiB for 35B-A3B (10 layers x 2 KV heads) and 64 KiB for 27B models (16 layers x 4 KV heads). A 128k context therefore needs about 4.0, 2.5 and 8.0 GiB respectively, plus a fixed DeltaNet recurrent state.

Qwen publishes official GGUF only for Qwen3 (2025), Qwen3-VL, Qwen3-Next-80B (2025-12-03) and Qwen3-Coder-Next (2026-02-02). Qwen publishes no GGUF for Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8; those come from ggml-org, unsloth, bartowski and lmstudio-community.
ggml-org/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF: Q4_K_M 20.5 GB, Q8_0 36.9 GB, plus an MTP draft (2.0 GB) and a DFlash draft (0.4 GB).
unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF: UD-Q3_K_XL 13.1 GB, UD-IQ4_XS 14.4 GB, UD-Q4_K_M 16.6 GB, UD-Q4_K_XL 17.7 GB, Q8_0 29.0 GB, mmproj-F16 0.9 GB.
Official Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-Next-GGUF: Q4_K_M 48.4 GB, Q5_K_M 56.7 GB, Q6_K 65.5 GB, Q8_0 84.8 GB.

llama.cpp has the architectures qwen35, qwen35moe, qwen3next and qwen4exp. llama-server offers --cpu-moe and --n-cpu-moe N to keep MoE expert weights in CPU RAM, --spec-type draft-mtp/draft-dflash, and OpenAI-style tool calling through --jinja, which is on by default. Latest release is b12418 (2026-11-15).

Ollama qwen3.8 lists only 27b tags: qwen3.8:27b (q4_K_M) 18 GB, q8_0 30 GB, 256K context, with vision, tools and thinking. qwen3.6:35b-a3b is 23 GB, qwen3.5:9b-q4_K_M 6.6 GB, qwen3.5:9b-q8_0 10 GB, qwen3-coder-next:q4_K_M 52 GB and qwen3-coder:30b 19 GB.
Qwen3.8-27B (vendor self-reported): Terminal Bench 2.1 (Terminus) 73.0 vs 63.4 for Qwen3.6-27B; SWE-bench Pro 61.7; LiveCodeBench v6 90.3; IFBench 79.5. The card gives no SWE-bench Verified number.
Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (vendor): SWE-bench Verified 73.4, Terminal-Bench 2.0 51.5, SWE-bench Pro 49.5, MCPMark 37.0. Qwen3.6-27B: SWE-bench Verified 77.2, Terminal-Bench 2.0 59.3.
Qwen3.5-9B (vendor): BFCL-V4 66.1, TAU2-Bench 79.1, LiveCodeBench v6 65.6. Qwen3.5-4B: BFCL-V4 50.3, TAU2 79.9.

Qwen3-Coder-Next tech report: SWE-bench Verified 70.6 (SWE-Agent), 71.1 (MiniSWE-Agent), 71.3 (OpenHands); SWE-bench Pro 44.3; Terminal-Bench 2.0 36.2 (Terminus2-json) and 30.9 (Claude Code scaffold); max 300 turns.
Qwen3-Coder-Next, Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct and Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 each state 'supports only non-thinking mode and does not generate <think></think> blocks'.
The Qwen3.8-27B chat_template.jinja uses <tool_call><function=...><parameter=...> XML tool calls (the qwen3_coder format) and reads enable_thinking, reasoning_effort and preserve_thinking.

Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 models have a native context of 262,144 tokens. YaRN with factor 4.0 extends this to about 1M through --hf-overrides on text_config.rope_parameters and VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1. Qwen warns that static YaRN can hurt quality on short texts.
Qwen3.8 recommended sampling. Thinking: temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 20, presence_penalty 0.0. Non-thinking: temperature 0.7, top_p 0.80, top_k 20, presence_penalty 1.5.
Qwen-AgentWorld-35B-A3B (2026-06-22) is a 'language world model' for simulating agent environments. It is not a coding assistant, and it needs --language-model-only in vLLM.

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next has 125B parameters with 6B active, plus 51B n-gram embeddings and 4B MTP (176B in total), under license qwen-community-1.0 (not Apache). Its smallest community GGUF is 66.4 GB, so it cannot run on this machine.

In vLLM on 16 GB with gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 (about 14.3 GiB), Qwen3.5-4B BF16 (9.3 GB) or a community 4-bit Qwen3.5-9B (9.1-9.4 GB) leaves roughly 3.5-4.5 GiB for KV. At 32 KiB/token that is about 110-140k tokens of context. This is not tested on hardware.
The Qwen readthedocs vLLM page still describes Qwen3-era usage: vllm>=0.8.5, --tool-call-parser hermes, --reasoning-parser qwen3 (since vLLM 0.9.0). It does not cover Qwen3.5+.

gaps: Qwen blog posts at qwen.ai and qwenlm.github.io/blog/qwen3-coder-next/ (404) could not be read; Coder-Next numbers come from the tech report PDF on GitHub.
Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct benchmarks are only in an image on the card and were not extracted.

No vendor-official 4-bit (AWQ/GPTQ/NVFP4) build exists for Qwen3.5-9B/4B or any Qwen3.6/3.8 size; the 4-bit options are third-party (RedHatAI, nvidia, Inferact, cyankiwi, AxionML, unsloth, ggml-org). Their quality was not verified.
Nothing in this run was benchmarked on the actual RTX 5080 Laptop: all KV and fit figures are arithmetic on config.json plus the recipe's RTX 5090 results, not measurements.
Throughput (tokens/s) with --n-cpu-moe for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Qwen3-Coder-Next on this CPU/RAM was not found in a primary source.
